challenge.title_es: Salto de longitud estilo Track & Field
challenge.prompt: Recreate the long jump event of the classic NES game Track & Field, with the best graphics you can manage in a single HTML file: a side-scrolling stadium with a runway, a take-off board, a sand pit with a measuring tape, a crowd in the stands, flags, scoreboard and sky. The athlete is an animated sprite that runs with a proper run cycle, leans, jumps in an arc, tucks and lands in the sand raising a puff of particles; the sand shows the landing mark. Classic mechanics: a speed bar that fills by alternating two keys, an angle selector that swings while running, a foul line that invalidates the jump if crossed, the distance measured in metres with one decimal, three attempts, a best mark and a world record line. Add a slow-motion replay of the jump and a results screen. Pixel art drawn procedurally in code (no external images), crisp nearest-neighbour scaling, animated details (crowd waving, flags, clouds) and a readable HUD.
challenge.excelente: Un estadio con público y detalle, un atleta con animación de carrera, salto y caída creíbles, barra de potencia y ángulo como en el original, marca medida en la arena con repetición a cámara lenta. Pixel art cuidado y con personalidad, que dan ganas de jugarlo.

rubric.es: Se ve una pista de carrerilla, la tabla de batida y un foso de arena
Hay un atleta con animación de carrera (no una figura que se desliza)
El atleta salta con arco y cae en la arena
Hay un indicador de velocidad o potencia que sube al correr
Hay un selector o indicador del ángulo de batida
Se mide la distancia del salto y aparece en metros
Hay público, gradas o banderas animadas de fondo
El dibujo es de píxeles nítidos y con detalle, no formas planas
La partida avanza sola, con saltos completos, sin que nadie pulse nada
Va fluido (al menos 30 fotogramas por segundo)

prompt:
Recreate the long jump event of the classic NES game Track & Field, with the best graphics you can manage in a single HTML file: a side-scrolling stadium with a runway, a take-off board, a sand pit with a measuring tape, a crowd in the stands, flags, scoreboard and sky. The athlete is an animated sprite that runs with a proper run cycle, leans, jumps in an arc, tucks and lands in the sand raising a puff of particles; the sand shows the landing mark. Classic mechanics: a speed bar that fills by alternating two keys, an angle selector that swings while running, a foul line that invalidates the jump if crossed, the distance measured in metres with one decimal, three attempts, a best mark and a world record line. Add a slow-motion replay of the jump and a results screen. Pixel art drawn procedurally in code (no external images), crisp nearest-neighbour scaling, animated details (crowd waving, flags, clouds) and a readable HUD.

Also include an autoplay demo mode toggled with the P key, in which the game plays itself competently (an AI controls the player) so a viewer can watch a good run.

The animation should show everything important within the first 30 seconds (that is the window we record); it may loop or continue after that.

Requirements: deliver everything in ONE self-contained HTML file (inline CSS and JavaScript; no external resources, CDNs, fonts or images). Reply with the complete file in a single ```html code block.

faults: (leve) La distancia mostrada en los paneles de resultado es '0.0 M' (capturas 12 y 13) incluso cuando se produce un salto, lo cual parece un error de lógica o de demo.
